UBS analyst Peter Grom lowered his 12-month price target to $70 from $78, representing approximately 40% upside from the stock's October 13 closing price of $50.10. In a research note Thursday titled "The Grass Is Looking Greener," Grom said the company's valuation has fallen to levels last observed in October 2023, reflecting excessive skepticism about its ability to deliver earnings growth.
The upgrade signals growing confidence that Scotts Miracle-Gro

can expand profitability even as inflation, elevated interest rates and a sluggish housing market weigh on consumer spending. UBS sees opportunities for earnings growth through productivity improvements, higher-margin products and pricing increases. The firm's bullish assessment follows a 25.7% decline in the stock relative to the broader market since the company's analyst day in early August.

Grom expects organic revenue growth of 2.2% in fiscal 2027 and 2.4% in fiscal 2028, exceeding Wall Street consensus estimates of 1.6% and 2%, respectively. UBS forecasts adjusted earnings per share of $4.76 in fiscal 2027, compared with consensus of $4.70, followed by $5.29 in fiscal 2028, above the Street's $5.13 estimate.
Consumer purchasing trends provide additional support for the upgrade. UBS analysis of Numerator data indicates that higher-income households now account for approximately 43% of Scotts Miracle-Gro's

sales, compared with 26% in 2019. The shift toward wealthier consumers could help insulate the company's brands from economic weakness and support further price increases. Meanwhile, younger consumers have emerged as a source of growth, particularly in indoor gardening and e-commerce.

The company's online business represents another expansion opportunity. Management previously reported that e-commerce point-of-sale revenue increased 22% during the first half of fiscal 2026, with online sales growing across every product category and customer. UBS also highlighted the company's strong brand positions, which provide pricing power in categories including lawn fertilizer, growing media and pest control.
Profitability remains central to Grom's investment thesis. Scotts Miracle-Gro

has expanded its gross margin from 26.3% in fiscal 2022 to an estimated 32.5% in fiscal 2026. UBS projects further improvement to 33% in fiscal 2027 and 33.9% in fiscal 2028, the latter exceeding consensus by 60 basis points. The firm expects productivity initiatives, favorable product mix and pricing to help offset inflationary pressures, which could approach the upper end of management's previously outlined $80 million range for fiscal 2027.
Valuation also strengthens the investment case. Scotts Miracle-Gro

trades at a 5.8% discount to small- and mid-cap household and personal care peers based on forward earnings, compared with its five-year average premium of 34.5%. UBS outlined a bullish scenario in which the stock reaches $92, while its downside scenario suggests a decline to $39. The firm's $70 base-case target incorporates a blend of earnings and enterprise-value multiples.

Risks remain, particularly from weaker consumer demand, higher commodity costs and unfavorable weather. UBS acknowledged that recent sales trends have been uneven, with weakness returning in August and September following a strong June and July. Nevertheless, Grom says the company's relatively resilient categories, increasingly affluent customer base and potential for sustained margin expansion make the stock's current risk-reward profile attractive.

title: Scotts Miracle-Gro climbs as UBS upgrades stock on valuation
